sections.content:
Probe results:
- Select the rightmost top dot (16,44): no ring (None). Interesting! In level 1, selecting a dot always displayed a ring in the direction of the nearest dot. Here, the rightmost dot (43) has its nearest dot at 31 → I was expecting a ring at 37. But no ring. Hmm, wait — maybe the ring only appears when the dot can actually move... or maybe the click at (16,44) didn't hit the dot? The dot is at rows 15-18, cols 43-46 → center (16.5, 44.5). (16,44) should hit. But no ring.
- Select the leftmost top (16,14): ring at (15,15,26,27) px=2 → rows 15-15, cols 26-27. This is the cell just past the dot at 19-22, i.e., the cell at cols 25-28 (ring at rows 15, cols 26-27 = partial ring). So the leftmost dot's ring is at 25-28, just past the dot at 19. ✓ Normal.
- Select the bottom dot (52,44): no ring.
So the rightmost top dot and the bottom dot don't display a ring. Why?
Hypothesis: the ring appears in the direction of the nearest dot, but only if that direction is "valid"... For the rightmost top dot (43): the nearest dot is 31 (left) → the ring should be at 37. But there's no ring. Hmm.
Alternative hypothesis: the ring only appears when the dot can move toward the nearest dot AND there's space... no, that's not it.
Wait, maybe I misread: the ring for the rightmost dot is at 37-40, but my ringpos() only detects g blobs with pixels ≤8. In level 1, the ring was a 4x4 hollow (about 12-16 px of g). Here the leftmost ring was px=2 (rows 15-15, cols 26-27) — a tiny fragment! So the ring rendering here is different (partial). For the rightmost dot, the ring might be a g blob with a different pixel count, or the ring might be at 37-40 but my filter missed it (px>8?).
Let me re-probe: select the rightmost dot, and enumerate all g nodes with their pixel counts and bounding boxes.
Also the bottom dot: enumerate all g nodes after selection.
Let's do that.
